Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City Telephone Number 925.1 1.48 • 925.8888 • 925.03.32 www.dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT UALRAD ATTY. HANS ROGER LUNA Municipal Legal Counsel Bangued, Abra Dear Atty. Luna: DILG OPINION NO. 20 S. 2013 24 MAY 2013 This has reference to your letter dated 04 May 2013 requesting for enlightenment on the following issues: "1. May this letter con taining an opinion be a legal basis for the Vice-Mayor to take his oath? 2. Is the absence of the Mayor by virtue of a warran t of' arrest be a valid reason that the ofFce of the mayor considered vacant? 3. Can you please explain to us Sec. 46 (a) of th e Loca I Government Code of 1991. " Since the issues raised are related, we shall answer them in one (I) discussion. Section 46 (a) of Republic Act No. 71602 provides and we quote: "Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) the governor, city or municipal temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. " (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the aforequoted provision of law, the vice-mayor shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive DILG-CAR Opinion No. 13-260. series of 2013. Otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991.

concerned when the latter is temporarily incapacitated to perform the same. Let it be noted that Section 46 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160 does not limit the grounds for temporary incapacity in the office of the local chief executive to those enumerated therein, such as leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Said provision uses the phrase "such as, but not limited to" which only implies other similar cases. 'The vice-mayor shall then assume as Acting Mayor who will be performing executive functions and cannot anymore preside over sessions of the sanggunian as long as the temporary incapacity of the incumbent mayor subsists. This is in accordance with the case of Gamboa vs. Aguirreg, where the Supreme Court ruled that the vice-governor, as Acting Governor, cannot anymore continue to preside over the session of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan as this would violate the principle of separation of powers and functions. The Supreme Court added that the vice-governor, in his capacity as Acting Governor, is expected to perform full-time executive functions that include the approval of ordinances or specific resolutions. Applying the foregoing in the case of Mayor Ryan Seares Luna and based on previous legal opinions4 rendered by the Department on similar set of facts, the Warrant of' Arrest issued by the RTC of Abra (Branch 2) against accused Mayor Luna coupled with his absence and non-performance of his duties and functions can be considered a "physical or legal reason" under Section 46 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160 which temporarily incapacitates him from performing his duties as Mayor of Bangued, Abra. For this, we find DILG-CAR Opinion No. 13-260, series of 2013 in order and that Vice-Mayor Allan P. Seares may already assume, but only in a temporary capacity, the office of the Municipal Mayor applying Section 46 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160. Said assumption of the vice-mayor is automatic or by operation of law and therefore needs no further overt act. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. V truly yours, AUSTERE A.
